result.title: Do Diffusion Models Learn to Generalize Basic Visual Skills?
result.summary: Diffusion models generate high-quality images, but how well they generalize is hard to measure. Current evaluations rely on human preference and prompt-following benchmarks for text-to-image models and on distribution-level metrics such as Fréchet Inception Distance (FID) and Inception Score (IS) for class-conditional models, but these cannot tell whether models learn basic visual skills or largely match training patterns. To address this gap, we introduce the Visual Generative Lab (VGL), a controlled experimental framework for studying how diffusion models learn and generalize basic visual skills, including size, position, rotation, count, color, shape, and their compositions. By generating synthetic training data for each skill from explicit rules, VGL allows precise measurement of generalization with task-specific, rule-based metrics. Training models from scratch on these data reveals three patterns in this controlled setting: (1) with our default design, extrapolation is limited: size and position degrade within a few pixels of the training range, count reaches only about 50% accuracy on out-of-range counts, and rotation extrapolation accuracy varies widely across seeds; (2) for compositional generalization, the number of distinct basic visual skill combinations matters more than dataset size; (3) skills mostly fail independently, except position. Code and data-generation scripts: https://github.com/AmishSethi/visual-generative-lab.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Visual Generative Lab 可控框架，用显式规则生成合成数据从头训练 diffusion 模型，按规则化指标测量 size、position、rotation、count、color、shape 及组合的泛化，发现外推普遍受限、组合泛化更依赖技能组合多样性而非数据量，且各技能多独立失败（position 除外）。
AI.relevance_reason: 属图像生成而非 VLM 推理，但其把视觉能力拆成可规则化度量的单项技能与组合、并检验外推与组合泛化的实验设计，可能可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节保留与组合泛化诊断的评测构造。
